title: Back pressure: when the queue keeps growing

kcs.statement: A new message waits roughly backlog size divided by drain rate, so an unbounded queue that keeps growing turns into unbounded latency and eventually memory exhaustion.

Back pressure bounds the queue and pushes the overload back to producers by blocking, slowing or rejecting them (for example HTTP 429 or 503 with Retry-After) instead of accepting work that cannot be finished in time.

problem_ideas: Backlog is 600,000 messages and consumers drain 2,000/s: how long does a new message wait?
